verdicts.why: Centres spite and resentment at another's success exactly as the gloss does, distinguishing it from mere wanting; negative charge fits.
Insatiable desire for wealth with a grasping, predatory force — inside the word, inside the gloss, negative fits.
Belligerence at real or supposed wrong given the solemn weight of a sin versus anger's mood — matches the gloss and stays on the word.
Overbearing pride shown as a superior manner toward inferiors, read as a flat accusation — the gloss's sense and a plausible negative.
Same overbearing pride as a chilly formal bearing above inferiors; register label is fine and the contrast with arrogance is about the word's force.
Explicitly the vice sense — self-esteem grown unreasonable and inordinate — and both examples show pride as a fault, not a virtue.
Earnest asking in a formal key, set against importune's repetition; matches 'plead or ask for earnestly' and neutral charge is plausible.
Entreaty raised to desperate pitch versus beg's flatness — a force description of supplication that fits the gloss.
Persistent urgent begging whose persistence burdens the person asked — this is what makes the charge negative, and the example fits.
Reads the begging sense of insist (as the example shows), locating force in refusing to drop the asking rather than in emotion; neutral is plausible.
The entreat sense in its most formal dress, not the religious one, and both examples are the 'pray forgive/pray tell' entreaty.
Humility made explicit and ceremonial versus beg's implied lowness — 'ask humbly' stated as the word's force.
Deception located wholly in the mimicked animal cry with no promise involved — exactly the gloss, neutral and technical, example fits.
Persuasion that sounds pleasant even when exaggerated — describes the word's force within the gloss's 'often false or exaggerated promises'.
Entice plus the trap closing, landing harder than entice — both halves of the gloss accounted for, negative fits.
Drawing the person along with the falseness of the promise nearest the surface — a force contrast within the synset, not a narrowing of the gloss.
Lightest of the three, a promise held out to someone still free of it; the Austen-style example is this persuasion sense and negative remains plausible.
Life and spirit rather than motion, with the 'with' construction the gloss itself flags; both examples fit this sense.
Lively action as vigorous springing, sturdier than bouncy — inside the gloss and the word, example fits.
Same lively spring taken lighter and more playful than bouncing — a force contrast, example fits.
Freshness beside animation making the liveliness light and easy — matches 'fresh and animated' and stays on the word.
High spirits caught rising, in motion where bubbly is a settled quality — the gloss's sense, positive fits.
Covers both being full of and showing high spirits, as the gloss's 'full of or showing' does; examples fit.
Enthusiasm in the voice with nothing holding it back — 'uttered with unrestrained enthusiasm' as force; positive with a hint of overflow is plausible.
Quality rather than burst, looser and more casual than burbling — register and force only, and the example is this sense.
Same high spirits in a polished formal register — a register label plus the gloss's sense, example fits.
High spirits granted but made to look light and easily dispersed — weakest approval in the family, positive still plausible for this gloss.
Life and energy stated plainly as the family's baseline — matches the gloss and all three examples fit.
